description: In store.rs::record_verifications, DnsError is serialised as 'domain\x00err' (NUL-separated). The code comments 'Domain names never contain NUL, so this is unambiguous.' DNS domain names from wire format cannot contain NUL, but the domain field of VerifResult::DnsError comes from identity.clone().unwrap_or_default() in dkim.rs, where identity is output.signature().map(|s| s.d.clone()). The mail-auth crate parses the 'd=' tag from a DKIM-Signature header. An attacker who controls the DKIM-Signature header (e.g. a relay that injects a header) could include a NUL byte in the d= value if mail-auth does not strip it. If a NUL ends up in the domain field, the NUL-split decode in parse_result will misparse the stored value, potentially associating the wrong domain with the error. Low-severity: affects logging/diagnosis only, not auth decisions.
title: verify: store.rs DnsError reason encoded as domain NUL err; NUL in domain breaks decode
